summary: This article explains how volcanoes form, why they erupt in different ways, how scientists watch them, and what the old lava fields of western Arabia tell us.
introduce: Draw two overlapping circles on the board and quickly compare two familiar things, such as a cat and a dog, with the class. Tell students that while reading “Volcanoes: Mountains of Fire” they will look for ways things are alike and different.

keyTerms.def: melted into a liquid by great heat
having to do with the huge moving pieces of the Earth's outer shell
bursting out suddenly and with great force

challengeTerms.def: the thin, hard outer layer of the Earth
thick and sticky, so it flows slowly
a scientist who studies rocks, the ground, and how the Earth changes

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that people should never live near a volcano? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Compare explosive eruptions and calm eruptions. What makes them different?
struggling: Read the first part of the article aloud together, review molten, tectonic, and explosive, and let weak readers fill in a T-chart of alike and different with sentence starters.
gifted: Ask strong readers to read a challenging version and write a short paragraph that uses crust, viscous, and geologist to compare two ideas from the article and explain which difference matters most.
